title: Work IQ: agents create and edit Office documents
summary: The roadmap facts, preview operations, licensing and both navigation paths are supported. The page nevertheless calls the default unstated despite the documented tenant-policy requirement for MCP writes, and treats server blocking as unconfirmed even though Microsoft says blocking an MCP server disables all its tools.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not said whether blocking Work IQ MCP in Tools stops this feature's document operations.
claims.quote: Blocking an MCP server disables all the tools it exposes. This action targets the server component, rather than a whole plugin package.
claims.fix: Remove the sentence 'Microsoft has not said whether blocking Work IQ MCP there stops the document operations in this feature.' The Office Document Tools page explicitly places these actions on Work IQ MCP, and https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers#block-or-allow-an-mcp-server says blocking a server disables all its exposed tools; this does not assert effects across other products or components.

claims.quote: These agents exclusively use Anthropic's AI models. This AI model must be enabled.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The document feature's default state is unknown because Microsoft has not stated what happens on arrival.
claims.quote: A separate tenant policy layer evaluates each tool request and blocks mutation operations by default. Administrators can enable supported create, update, delete, and action requests through tenant policy.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to 'admin-opt-in'. Replace 'Microsoft has not stated what happens on arrival' with 'For the documented Work IQ MCP preview, document mutation requests are blocked by default; an administrator must enable supported write scenarios through tenant policy.' Replace the first Open questions bullet with 'Does our tenant policy currently allow the preview document mutation requests?' Keep the Copilot Studio quotation explicitly scoped to that experience and its qualification that organisational policies still apply; it does not establish an exception to the documented MCP policy layer. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/mcp/tool-reference and the already cited Office Document Tools page.
